name.description:
Display name the agent itself gave this session, when the agent
publishes one and it has been resolved. Additive and optional: absent
for agents that publish no such name, and for sessions not yet resolved.

oneOf.description:
A growth guardrail refused or truncated a proposal.

The only new event kind in Phase 2: an accepted proposal already emits
`workflow.node.created`, whose `WorkflowRunNodeInfo` carries
`parent_path` and `depth`, so a second "spawned" event would give
clients two events for one fact. What no client can derive is the node
that was asked for and never created.

The epilogue's summary was accepted and enqueued
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1). There is no second `workflow.run.finished`
and no `workflow.run.updated` — the run's status was already final.

One watchdog rung fired against a node
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.4). Carries the node as of
the intervention, so a subscriber sees `watchdog_interventions` and
`attention` without a second `workflow.run.get` round trip.
A review cycle began (`workflow.review.start`).

A review cycle finished synthesis and is waiting on the human's
per-finding accept.

A review cycle reached a terminal status: `applied`, `declined`, or
`failed`.

WorkflowAttention.description:
[`WorkflowRunNodeInfo::attention`]'s fixed vocabulary, mirroring the
`run_node.attention` store ASSERT
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.7).

oneOf.description:
The owner's pane has been idle for `stuck_threshold` samples while its
task stayed `in_progress`, and the watchdog ladder ran out of rungs.

The node's authored `timeout_ms` was exceeded; jumps straight to
surfaced without walking the nudge/re-prompt rungs.

The owner's pane is `needs input`, or the task is `blockedBy` an
unfinished task — a human, not a nudge, unblocks this.
The lead's own pane is `needs input`, which blocks the whole run.
The run never bound a team within the bind deadline.

WorkflowDemand.description: How demanding a node's work is; drives the tier's model/effort mapping.

WorkflowEvidence.description:
Which completion signal was accepted for a node
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §4.3).

WorkflowGrowthLimit.description:
One growth guardrail being reached, in the one shape reused by
[`WorkflowRunInfo`], [`WorkflowRunNodeInfo`], the `workflow.growth.limited`
event, and the CLI renderers.

accepted.description:
How many of `requested` were created anyway. Non-zero means partial
acceptance, which is the interesting case: the shortfall is reported
rather than silently truncated.

limit_value.description: The ceiling's value, so a reader does not have to look it up.

oneOf.description:
The proposing node's own `expand_max`, counted cumulatively across every
proposal it has made in this run.
The run's `max_depth`, guarded as `parent.depth + 1 <= max_depth`.

The run's `max_nodes`, counted over every materialised node regardless
of status — a failed child does not refund budget.

WorkflowInterrogationInfo.description:
A live or ended interrogation of a past node's Claude session
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D7-D8). Not a `run_node`: interrogations have their
own lifecycle and are never counted toward a run's node totals.

forked_session_id.description:
Learned from the pane's session report when not pre-assigned at spawn
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D7).

path.description: The source node's instance path, not the interrogation's own identity.

WorkflowRestoredFrom.description:
Provenance of a restored node, carried on `WorkflowRunNodeInfo`
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D4).

WorkflowReviewInfo.description:
A run's self-improvement review cycle, as the wire sees it
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md`, `.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.5).

evidence_only_count.description:
How many of this cycle's interviews degraded to `evidence_only`
because no session could be resumed — surfaced so "the review ran"
and "the review heard from everyone" are never conflated.

interview_paths.description:
One path per interview this cycle conducted (the interrogation's
transcript, source or forked as `interview_mode` says).

resulting_version_id.description: Set once `workflow.review.apply` compiles and mints a new version.

WorkflowReviewStatus.description:
The self-improvement review cycle's status
(`store/migrations/0001_init.surql`'s `review_cycle.status` ASSERT).

context_runs.description:
Source runs whose summaries this run's nodes were offered via
`context/prior-runs.md` (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D21).

growth_limited.description: The run's most recent growth limit, if any.

lead_pane_id.description: The lead's own pane, which is where a user steers the whole run.

lead_prompt_version.description:
Which version of karvex's rendered lead prompt started this run, so a
stored run says what contract produced it.

lead_session_id.description:
The Claude Code session id of the run's team lead
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.1). Absent for a run that predates the
agent-teams rework, and until karvex has recognised the lead's team.

max_depth.description:
The run's **effective** growth ceilings — the version's, narrowed by the
tier. One authority: what the run graph enforces is what the run row
persists and what this reports.

nodes_live.description:
Nodes materialised so far, counted against `max_nodes` regardless of
status.

restore_from_run.description: The run this one restored checkpoints from, if any.

team_name.description:
The team the lead created, `session-` plus the first eight characters
of its session id. The key both `~/.claude/tasks/<team>/` and
`~/.claude/teams/<team>/` are addressed by.

workflow_name.description:
Denormalised so a cross-workflow run list can label a row without N
extra calls (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D9).

assignment_reason.description:
Why `model`/`effort` read what they read — the `auto` tier's reason
string, empty for a fixed tier whose table row is the explanation.

attention.description:
A karvex-owned verdict about why this node needs a human, distinct
from Claude Code's own projected `status`
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §6 D-10). `None` means the
watchdog has nothing to report, which includes both "healthy" and "the
watchdog has not looked yet".

Landed as shape in wave 0 (packet P3) ahead of its store column and
writer, which the watchdog packet (wave 2b) adds — this field reads
`None` on every run until then, honestly, because nothing sets it yet
rather than because it is faked healthy.

delivery_failure.description:
The last pane delivery the runtime refused for this node, e.g. a steer
whose keystrokes never reached the process. A shared runtime fact, so it
belongs on the API and not only in TUI state.

emergent.description:
Whether the team created this task without the definition planning it.
Emergent nodes are first-class rather than hidden — the loose part of
the contract, recorded.

growth_limited.description: The last growth limit this node ran into as a *proposer*.

label.description:
The node's own name: an expansion child's accepted `--label`, or the
authored kvdag label for a static node. A property of the *instance*,
not of `node_key` — a generation cut from one template shares the key,
so a reader that names nodes by key names them all the same
(`04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §3.4, 2026-08-08 amendment). A shared
runtime fact, so it belongs on the API and not only in TUI state.

owner.description:
The teammate that claimed the task, empty while unclaimed. Its pane is
in the run's member list, which is what makes "select a node, focus the
pane that owns it" resolvable.

restored_from.description:
Provenance when this node was seeded from a past run's checkpoint
rather than executed (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D4).

subject.description:
The observed task subject, verbatim. Kept beside `label` rather than
replacing it: `label` is what the definition called the node, and this
is what the team actually called the work.

task_id.description:
Claude Code's own task id for this node, once the run projection has
seen a task matching it (`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.4). Absent on an
engine-era run and on a planned node no task has claimed yet.

transcript_path.description:
The transcript path a workflow pane's session report last confirmed
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D6). `None` means no session ever reported one
— interrogation falls back to the pre-launch estimate.

WorkflowRunSummaryInfo.description:
A completed run's epilogue-authored summary
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1, D10). `summary.get` returning `None` and this
type being absent from a `summary.list` result both mean the same normal
thing: no summary was written, never an error.

run_pruned.description:
Set once the source run is pruned; the summary itself is the one
never-pruned row (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D9).

WorkflowSuccession.description:
Every closing node records exactly one of these
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §3.3).

WorkflowSummaryNodeLine.description:
One node's line in a run summary's per-node breakdown
(`04-kvdag-and-execution.md`'s epilogue schema, `07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1).

timeout_ms.description: Startup timeout in milliseconds. Values must be greater than 3000 and at most 300000.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

WorkflowDefinitionDocument.description:
A kvdag definition document: TOML or JSON, in the shape
`docs/design/workflow-builder/05-phase-plan.md` §4 documents. See the
module doc for why this is opaque text rather than a typed node/edge tree.

WorkflowInterrogationMode.description:
Which spawn shape `workflow.node.interrogate` uses.
`Resumed` forks the source Claude session (`03-storage-schema.md` §4.4);
`Reconstructed` seeds a fresh session from the stored checkpoint when no
transcript is available, and is always explicitly labelled as such —
never presented as the original teammate
(`00-overview.md` Feature 3, `07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D7).

WorkflowNodeExpandParams.description:
A node proposing new nodes
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §3.4).

Token-authenticated exactly like [`WorkflowNodeReportParams`]: an expand
proposal is a node speaking, not an operator. A *rejected* proposal is a
successful response carrying the rejection — the run continues; only a bad
run/path/token or a closed run is an error.

count.description:
How many children to instantiate; defaults to 1. `u32` on the wire and
`u16` internally, so the handler narrows with `u16::try_from` and
rejects an out-of-range value rather than truncating it.

inputs.description:
Slot overrides for the template's `prompt_template`. A key naming no
declared slot is rejected rather than ignored: this is an override
channel over the one validated renderer, never a second unvalidated one.

template.description: The kvdag key of the template to instantiate.

WorkflowNodeReportParams.description:
The node self-report contract
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §4.3): token-
authenticated with `KARVEX_WORKFLOW_NODE_TOKEN`, precedence 1 of the three
completion signals.

WorkflowRestoreRequest.description:
A `workflow.run` request asking to seed some nodes from a past run's
checkpoints instead of re-executing them (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D3, D11).
A bare `nodes: []` means every restorable node of the source run
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D18).

WorkflowReviewAnswerParams.description:
One interview pane's self-report (`kvx workflow review answer`), from its
own pane — authorised exactly like [`WorkflowRunFinishParams`]: possession
of the run id plus `KARVEX_WORKFLOW_REVIEW_INTERVIEW`, the env var karvex
exported into that specific interview pane, checked against `member` so a
pane can only ever answer for the interview it was spawned to conduct.

answer.description:
The answer JSON itself. Exactly one of this and `answer_file` is
required, the same split `WorkflowRunFinishParams` uses and for the
same reason: the interviewer writes JSON to
`<cycle dir>/answers/<member>.json` and should not have to inline it
through argv.

member.description: The team-roster name this interview was conducted with.

WorkflowReviewApplyParams.description:
`workflow.review.start` / `workflow.review.get` share `WorkflowRunTarget`
(reused, `run_id`) — there is at most one review cycle per run at a time.

`workflow.review.apply` — everything not in `accept` is declined; an empty
`accept` declines the whole cycle.

accept.description:
Finding `node_key`s to accept. Every finding this cycle produced that
is not named here is declined.

WorkflowReviewReportParams.description:
The synthesis pane's self-report (`kvx workflow review report --file
findings.json`), authorised the same way
[`WorkflowReviewAnswerParams`] is.

findings.description:
The findings JSON itself. Exactly one of this and `findings_file` is
required.

WorkflowRunFinishParams.description:
The team lead's own end-of-run report (`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.3).

Authorised by possession of the run id: karvex puts `KARVEX_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID`
in the lead's pane, so `kvx workflow run finish` needs no argument and
nothing that has not been handed the run can close it.

outcome.description:
A one-word verdict for the run. Defaults to `succeeded`; a lead that
concluded the run could not finish says so here and still calls finish.

summary.description:
The summary text itself. Exactly one of this and `summary_file` is
required; the file form exists because a lead writes markdown to disk
and should not have to inline it through argv.

workflow_id.description:
`None` lists runs across every workflow, newest first
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D9).

WorkflowRunMessageParams.description:
Sending text into one of a live run's Claude Code sessions
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.5a).

A runtime capability, not a UI feature: the target is named by the same
roster `workflow.run.get` publishes, and the transport is Claude Code's own
documented per-session inbox socket.

priority.description:
`now`, `next` (the default), or `later` — Claude Code's own queue
vocabulary for when the receiving session reads the message.

target.description: The session to reach, by team-roster name. `team-lead` is the run's lead.

args.description:
Materialised into `workflow_run.args`; fills the declared `ArgSpec`
namespace (`kvx workflow run start … --arg k=v`).

include_prior_summaries.description:
Defaults to `true` when absent (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D21): the run's
nodes read prior runs' summaries via `context/prior-runs.md` unless
explicitly opted out.

restore_from.description:
Seed some nodes from a past run's checkpoints instead of re-executing
them (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D3, D11).

version.description: Defaults to the workflow's head version.

WorkflowRunReportSessionParams.description:
One of a run's Claude Code sessions identifying itself
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.1a).

Posted by the `SessionStart` hook karvex puts in the run's `--settings`, so
the run's team is an assertion from the session rather than something karvex
infers from file timestamps. Authorised the same way
[`WorkflowRunFinishParams`] is — possession of the run id, which karvex bakes
into the hook command — and checked against the pane id karvex itself put in
the pane's environment.

agent_id.description:
Set when the hook ran for an in-process subagent rather than for the
session itself, which is never an identity assertion.

messaging_socket.description:
`CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, the session's inbox. Absent when the
messaging feature flag had not resolved by the time the hook ran.

pane_id.description:
`KARVEX_PANE_ID`. The lead's pane binds the run; any other pane of this
run is a split-pane teammate.

session_id.description: The Claude Code session id, from the hook payload.

source.description:
Claude Code's own word for why the session started: `startup`, `resume`,
`clear`, …

name.description:
Display name the agent itself gave this session, when the agent
publishes one and it has been resolved. Additive and optional: absent
for agents that publish no such name, and for sessions not yet resolved.

oneOf.description:
A growth guardrail refused or truncated a proposal.

The only new event kind in Phase 2: an accepted proposal already emits
`workflow.node.created`, whose `WorkflowRunNodeInfo` carries
`parent_path` and `depth`, so a second "spawned" event would give
clients two events for one fact. What no client can derive is the node
that was asked for and never created.

The epilogue's summary was accepted and enqueued
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1). There is no second `workflow.run.finished`
and no `workflow.run.updated` — the run's status was already final.

One watchdog rung fired against a node
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.4). Carries the node as of
the intervention, so a subscriber sees `watchdog_interventions` and
`attention` without a second `workflow.run.get` round trip.
A review cycle began (`workflow.review.start`).

A review cycle finished synthesis and is waiting on the human's
per-finding accept.

A review cycle reached a terminal status: `applied`, `declined`, or
`failed`.

warnings.description:
Warnings collected at link time or on registry load (e.g. unknown event names,
missing manifest file). Non-fatal — the entry is kept and surfaced by plugin.list.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

detail.description:
The one projection both the human renderer and `--json` read, added
as a sibling rather than replacing `workflow` so no published
response field changes shape.

oneOf.description:
The team lead's own end-of-run report was accepted
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.3). Carries the closed run and the
summary as stored, so the caller sees exactly what was recorded.

A run session's self-report was recorded (`09-agent-teams-rework.md`
§3.1a). `role` says what the report was taken to be; an `Ignored` report
is a successful response, because a hook that fires for somebody else's
session is normal traffic rather than an error.

addressable.description: Whether the session reported a usable inbox socket.

team_name.description:
The team the reporting lead's session id names, so a caller can see
the derivation karvex applied.

oneOf.description:
A message was written into a run session's inbox
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.5a).

A rejected proposal is a **successful** response carrying the rejection:
the run continues, and `rejected` being non-empty while `accepted` is
too is the partial-acceptance case.

accepted.description: Instance paths of the children the proposal created.

oneOf.description:
`None` means "no summary was written" — a normal answer, not an error
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1, D10).
A review cycle was started (`workflow.review.start`).

`workflow.review.get`'s answer. `review: None` means this run has
never had a review cycle — a normal answer, not an error, matching
`WorkflowSummaryGet`'s precedent.

The human's per-finding accept (`workflow.review.apply`) was recorded.
`version_id` is set only when at least one accepted finding compiled
and minted a new `kvdag_version`; an all-declined apply is a
successful response with `version_id: None`.

An interview pane's self-report was recorded
(`workflow.review.answer`).

The synthesis pane's self-report was recorded
(`workflow.review.report`), moving the cycle to `awaiting_user`.

WorkflowAttention.description:
[`WorkflowRunNodeInfo::attention`]'s fixed vocabulary, mirroring the
`run_node.attention` store ASSERT
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.7).

oneOf.description:
The owner's pane has been idle for `stuck_threshold` samples while its
task stayed `in_progress`, and the watchdog ladder ran out of rungs.

The node's authored `timeout_ms` was exceeded; jumps straight to
surfaced without walking the nudge/re-prompt rungs.

The owner's pane is `needs input`, or the task is `blockedBy` an
unfinished task — a human, not a nudge, unblocks this.
The lead's own pane is `needs input`, which blocks the whole run.
The run never bound a team within the bind deadline.

WorkflowDemand.description: How demanding a node's work is; drives the tier's model/effort mapping.

WorkflowDetail.description:
One projection of a workflow and its head document, read by **both**
`workflow.get`'s human renderer and its `--json` path so the two cannot
describe different field sets.

It arrives as a new sibling field on `ResponseResult::WorkflowGet` rather
than replacing that response's existing `workflow: WorkflowSummary`:
re-typing a published response field is the one change in this phase that
would be wire-incompatible, and every other addition is additive
self-describing JSON, which is what keeps `PROTOCOL_VERSION` where it is.

`description` comes from the `workflow` row, which `create_version` keeps
equal to the head document — `kvdag_version` has no `description` column, so
"read it from the head version" is not implementable.

WorkflowEdgePayload.description: How much of the source node's checkpoint is handed to the target.

WorkflowEvidence.description:
Which completion signal was accepted for a node
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §4.3).

limit.description:
The guardrail hit, when the rejection is a limit rather than a
validation failure.

WorkflowExpandRejectionReason.description: Why one proposal was refused, in whole or in part.

oneOf.description: The template is not in the proposing node's `expand_allow`.
No kvdag node carries that key.
The key names a node that is not declared `is_template`.
Partial acceptance: some children were created and the rest did not fit.
An `inputs` key naming no declared slot in the template.

WorkflowGrowthLimit.description:
One growth guardrail being reached, in the one shape reused by
[`WorkflowRunInfo`], [`WorkflowRunNodeInfo`], the `workflow.growth.limited`
event, and the CLI renderers.

accepted.description:
How many of `requested` were created anyway. Non-zero means partial
acceptance, which is the interesting case: the shortfall is reported
rather than silently truncated.

limit_value.description: The ceiling's value, so a reader does not have to look it up.

oneOf.description:
The proposing node's own `expand_max`, counted cumulatively across every
proposal it has made in this run.
The run's `max_depth`, guarded as `parent.depth + 1 <= max_depth`.

The run's `max_nodes`, counted over every materialised node regardless
of status — a failed child does not refund budget.

WorkflowInterrogationInfo.description:
A live or ended interrogation of a past node's Claude session
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D7-D8). Not a `run_node`: interrogations have their
own lifecycle and are never counted toward a run's node totals.

forked_session_id.description:
Learned from the pane's session report when not pre-assigned at spawn
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D7).

path.description: The source node's instance path, not the interrogation's own identity.

WorkflowIsolation.description: Working-directory isolation for a node's pane.

WorkflowMemberState.description:
[`WorkflowRunMemberInfo::last_state`]'s vocabulary — deliberately its own
enum rather than a shared "pane state" type (module doc: self-contained by
design), and deliberately not [`WorkflowNodeStatus`]: a member's own agent
state and the task it owns are two different facts that can disagree,
which is precisely what the watchdog's `LocalLoop` class detects.

WorkflowNodeKind.description:
What a node *is*. Orthogonal to [`WorkflowRunner`], which selects how it
is bound to a process.

WorkflowRestoreReport.description:
A restore's outcome, carried on `workflow.run`'s response
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D11). An all-skipped restore is a successful run
start with a fully populated `skipped` list, not an error.

restored.description: Instance paths of the nodes seeded from the source run's checkpoints.

WorkflowRestoreSkipReason.description:
Why one selector's restore did not happen. `definition_changed` is
bypassable with `allow_changed`; the other two never are
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D11, D19).

WorkflowRestoredFrom.description:
Provenance of a restored node, carried on `WorkflowRunNodeInfo`
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D4).

WorkflowReviewFindingInfo.description:
One finding a review cycle produced, as the wire sees it. Findings are
recorded wholesale and applied selectively: `accepted` says what
`workflow.review.apply` actually folded into the compiled version.

applied_in_version.description: Set once this finding's change is folded into a compiled version.

evidence.description:
Measured, not asserted: watchdog interventions, idle time, tokens,
tool uses, duration, schema failures — the numbers put to the
teammate, carried back so a reader can see what the verdict answers.

interrogation_id.description:
The `interrogation` row this finding came out of; absent only when the
interview was `evidence_only`.

proposed_change.description: The concrete change: a prompt rewrite, or a node-field delta.

replacement.description:
Mandatory when `verdict` is `replace`: a full replacement role
definition.

run_path.description:
The run node this finding is about, when it is about one specific
instance rather than the run/lead as a whole.

WorkflowReviewFindingLevel.description:
Whether a finding is a prompt-level tweak or a structural change to the
node's own definition (`review_finding.level` ASSERT).

WorkflowReviewInfo.description:
A run's self-improvement review cycle, as the wire sees it
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md`, `.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.5).

evidence_only_count.description:
How many of this cycle's interviews degraded to `evidence_only`
because no session could be resumed — surfaced so "the review ran"
and "the review heard from everyone" are never conflated.

interview_paths.description:
One path per interview this cycle conducted (the interrogation's
transcript, source or forked as `interview_mode` says).

resulting_version_id.description: Set once `workflow.review.apply` compiles and mints a new version.

WorkflowReviewInterviewMode.description:
Whether one finding came from the teammate's own forked-session account,
or was inferred from evidence alone because no session could be resumed
(`store/migrations/0001_init.surql`'s `review_finding.interview_mode`
ASSERT). The honesty rule survives verbatim from `08`: a finding never
claims a teammate's account it does not have.

WorkflowReviewStatus.description:
The self-improvement review cycle's status
(`store/migrations/0001_init.surql`'s `review_cycle.status` ASSERT).

WorkflowReviewVerdict.description:
The interviewer's verdict on one node's role (`review_finding.verdict`
ASSERT). `Replace` without a `replacement` is refused by the store
(`0001_init.surql`'s `review_finding_replace_requires_replacement` event)
and, ahead of that, by the handler.

members.description:
The run's team, newest observation first seen order. Empty for a run
that predates the agent-teams rework.

messaging.description:
Whether the run's sessions can be messaged, and which of them have
identified themselves. Present only for the run that is live on this
server: a messaging socket belongs to a running process, so a stored run
has nothing to report here.

context_runs.description:
Source runs whose summaries this run's nodes were offered via
`context/prior-runs.md` (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D21).

growth_limited.description: The run's most recent growth limit, if any.

lead_pane_id.description: The lead's own pane, which is where a user steers the whole run.

lead_prompt_version.description:
Which version of karvex's rendered lead prompt started this run, so a
stored run says what contract produced it.

lead_session_id.description:
The Claude Code session id of the run's team lead
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.1). Absent for a run that predates the
agent-teams rework, and until karvex has recognised the lead's team.

max_depth.description:
The run's **effective** growth ceilings — the version's, narrowed by the
tier. One authority: what the run graph enforces is what the run row
persists and what this reports.

nodes_live.description:
Nodes materialised so far, counted against `max_nodes` regardless of
status.

restore_from_run.description: The run this one restored checkpoints from, if any.

team_name.description:
The team the lead created, `session-` plus the first eight characters
of its session id. The key both `~/.claude/tasks/<team>/` and
`~/.claude/teams/<team>/` are addressed by.

workflow_name.description:
Denormalised so a cross-workflow run list can label a row without N
extra calls (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D9).

WorkflowRunMemberInfo.description:
One member of the run's Claude Code team, as karvex last observed it
(`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.4).

Snapshotted rather than read live: Claude Code deletes the team config when
the lead session ends, so this is the durable record of who worked on the
run and in which pane.

last_state.description:
The last pane agent state karvex observed for this member's owner
pane, so a finished run can still say how long a teammate sat idle
while its task stayed `in_progress`. `None` for the in-process lead
(no pane) or before any state has been observed.

Landed as shape in wave 0 (packet P3); populated starting with P8's
member-identity capture.

pane_id.description:
The member's karvex pane, for a split-pane teammate. Absent for the
in-process lead, which is a session rather than a pane.

session_id.description:
This member's own Claude Code session id, captured while the run was
alive (`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §3.3) — `members[]` never
carries one, and the config dir it lived in can vanish once the
session ends. Absent means karvex never resolved one for this member,
which makes that member `evidence_only` forever in a review — an
honest, visible outcome rather than a silent one.

Landed as shape in wave 0 (packet P3); populated starting with P8's
member-identity capture.

WorkflowRunMessageReceipt.description:
What karvex knows after handing a message to a session's inbox.

Deliberately not "delivered": the receiving session's inbound controls
decide between delivered, held, and refused *after* the write, and that
verdict travels back only to another Claude Code session's reply address.

channel.description:
`inbox_socket` for Claude Code's own peer channel, `pane_input` when
karvex typed it into the session's pane instead. Not equivalent: an
inbox message arrives labelled as another session's and is subject to
the receiver's inbound controls, while pane input is indistinguishable
from the user typing. Pane input is the fallback for a session whose
messaging token karvex does not hold — including every session of a run
that outlived a karvex restart, because a teammate's token exists
nowhere but that teammate's own hook environment.

WorkflowRunMessageTargetInfo.description: One session of a live run that karvex can address.

addressable.description:
Whether the session reported an inbox socket, and therefore whether a
message to it travels over Claude Code's own peer channel. A session can
identify itself without one — the messaging feature flag had not
resolved when its hook ran — and is then reached by pane input instead.

channel.description:
Which channel a message to this target would use today: `inbox_socket`
or `pane_input`.

name.description: The team-roster name, which is what `workflow.run.message` takes.

WorkflowRunMessagingInfo.description:
Whether this run's sessions can be messaged at all, and who is reachable.

Reported rather than assumed, because upstream is explicit that a kill
switch leaves cross-session messaging off with no visible difference in the
session — so a client that showed a message affordance regardless would be
offering a verb that silently does nothing.

detail.description:
The same reason as a sentence, for a client that has nowhere to put a
code.

reason.description:
A stable word for what karvex noticed: `claude_too_old`,
`unsupported_platform`, or `kill_switch_suspected`. Absent only when
there was nothing to report.

supported.description:
Whether karvex expects a message to this run's sessions to arrive.

`true` alongside a `reason` of `kill_switch_suspected` is a real
combination and not a contradiction: the variable that can disable
cross-session messaging only does so on an account whose Claude Code
feature flags have never been fetched, which karvex cannot see from
here, so it tries anyway and says what it noticed.

assignment_reason.description:
Why `model`/`effort` read what they read — the `auto` tier's reason
string, empty for a fixed tier whose table row is the explanation.

attention.description:
A karvex-owned verdict about why this node needs a human, distinct
from Claude Code's own projected `status`
(`.local/prd/phase4-retarget-plan.md` §6 D-10). `None` means the
watchdog has nothing to report, which includes both "healthy" and "the
watchdog has not looked yet".

Landed as shape in wave 0 (packet P3) ahead of its store column and
writer, which the watchdog packet (wave 2b) adds — this field reads
`None` on every run until then, honestly, because nothing sets it yet
rather than because it is faked healthy.

delivery_failure.description:
The last pane delivery the runtime refused for this node, e.g. a steer
whose keystrokes never reached the process. A shared runtime fact, so it
belongs on the API and not only in TUI state.

emergent.description:
Whether the team created this task without the definition planning it.
Emergent nodes are first-class rather than hidden — the loose part of
the contract, recorded.

growth_limited.description: The last growth limit this node ran into as a *proposer*.

label.description:
The node's own name: an expansion child's accepted `--label`, or the
authored kvdag label for a static node. A property of the *instance*,
not of `node_key` — a generation cut from one template shares the key,
so a reader that names nodes by key names them all the same
(`04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §3.4, 2026-08-08 amendment). A shared
runtime fact, so it belongs on the API and not only in TUI state.

owner.description:
The teammate that claimed the task, empty while unclaimed. Its pane is
in the run's member list, which is what makes "select a node, focus the
pane that owns it" resolvable.

restored_from.description:
Provenance when this node was seeded from a past run's checkpoint
rather than executed (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D4).

subject.description:
The observed task subject, verbatim. Kept beside `label` rather than
replacing it: `label` is what the definition called the node, and this
is what the team actually called the work.

task_id.description:
Claude Code's own task id for this node, once the run projection has
seen a task matching it (`09-agent-teams-rework.md` §3.4). Absent on an
engine-era run and on a planned node no task has claimed yet.

transcript_path.description:
The transcript path a workflow pane's session report last confirmed
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D6). `None` means no session ever reported one
— interrogation falls back to the pre-launch estimate.

WorkflowRunSummaryInfo.description:
A completed run's epilogue-authored summary
(`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1, D10). `summary.get` returning `None` and this
type being absent from a `summary.list` result both mean the same normal
thing: no summary was written, never an error.

run_pruned.description:
Set once the source run is pruned; the summary itself is the one
never-pruned row (`07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D9).

WorkflowRunner.description: Selects the binding the spawner uses for a node.

WorkflowSessionRole.description: What a session's self-report was taken to mean.

oneOf.description: The run's team lead. Binds the run.
Another session of the same run, in one of its panes.
Not this run's, or not a session.

WorkflowSuccession.description:
Every closing node records exactly one of these
(`docs/design/workflow-builder/04-kvdag-and-execution.md` §3.3).

WorkflowSummaryNodeLine.description:
One node's line in a run summary's per-node breakdown
(`04-kvdag-and-execution.md`'s epilogue schema, `07-phase3-plan.md` §4 D1).

WorkflowVersionOrigin.description: How a kvdag version came to exist.
